scope: Read-only attribution of the previously reported B32/T4 CPU-native residual; no performance-code change or new benchmark.

conclusion.summary: The diagnostic confirms cheaper overlap admission and a changed peak-reduction workload. The positive cProfile difference is concentrated in unchanged native FFTW plan execution and batch orchestration own time, while correlation and complete peak-helper cumulative time decrease. Opposite Torch-profile timing direction prevents assigning the original roughly 6% throughput regression to a single cause.
supported: Overlap comparisons and admission overhead are reduced.
Chunked peak arithmetic removes the sum/fill reduction and increases small-operation launches; argmax costs more in this one Torch profile.
Unchanged FFTW implementation dominates both cProfile samples.
not_supported: Claiming chunking, FFTW itself, scheduling, cache effects, or Python overhead conclusively causes the repeatable throughput loss.
Claiming the original 5.85% rate loss was remeasured for candidate-v2.
conclusion.next_action: No automatic performance change. Retain this attribution and the original timing result with their separate source identities.

source_identity.candidate_vs_v2_cpu_peak_note: The read-only diff preserves CPU chunk-size calculation, real.square()+imag.square(), per-chunk argmax, indexing and concatenation. It moves non-CPU handling outside the loop; source trees are nevertheless distinct.

baseline.accounting: Self time subtracts direct same-thread cpu_op children from each duration. These are host operation intervals, including waiting for worker threads, not summed physical-core CPU utilization. The trace span includes profiler context overhead. Opaque native FFTW/correlation and Python work are absent from cpu_op events.

candidate-v2.accounting: Self time subtracts direct same-thread cpu_op children from each duration. These are host operation intervals, including waiting for worker threads, not summed physical-core CPU utilization. The trace span includes profiler context overhead. Opaque native FFTW/correlation and Python work are absent from cpu_op events.

limitations: The unprofiled 0.94150448 paired rate ratio belongs to original candidate 97bf1614/tree d9819f6f. Diagnostic profiles use candidate-v2 0d005812/tree fa7a7c09. Matching CPU arithmetic and unchanged FFT/correlation implementations do not make these a fresh candidate-v2 throughput measurement.

One warm cProfile call per source and one separate Torch-profile call per source provide attribution samples, not variance estimates or statistically isolated causes. cProfile captures call 7, block 0; Torch profiler captures call 8, block 1. Both belong to the first warm measured iteration after one cold pass and one warmup across three different synthetic blocks.

Instrumentation perturbs timing. cProfile and Torch profiling have opposite overall direction here. Do not combine their milliseconds, subtract operator times from cProfile times, or interpret the instrumented worker throughput as a benchmark.

cProfile self time includes untraced native calls and uninstrumented expression/operator/deallocation work charged to their Python caller; it is not pure Python instruction time. The same-thread Torch trace does not expose native FFTW/correlation internals, four-core utilization, scheduler waits, cache behavior, or memory bandwidth.
The profiler used record_shapes=True but did not request memory profiling. Input element counts establish work/chunk sizes; they do not measure peak allocated memory or allocation traffic.

This is the synthetic public LiveBatchMatchedFilter component with FFT size 131072, batch 32, four configured threads, and affinity CPUs 8-11. It is not a compressed-bank pycbc_inspiral production-search measurement. Native-enabled here enables correlation and FFTW; optional native CPU peak selection is not enabled.
